notes.1a: This was generally well answered. The correct phrase ‘atoms of the same element with...’ was often reduced to ‘elements with...’.
notes.1c: The majority of candidates calculated the A value correctly. The number of significant figures quoted in the candidates’ answer should have been 4, the same as the data in the question. Information about significant figures and rounding up or down is given in Section 1
notes.1d: This was generally well answered, common errors being the use of 2Cl, rather than Cl , for chlorine or MgCl for the product.
notes.1e: Correct answers of 0.020 mol of Sb reacting with 0.060 mol of Cl atoms to give A as SbCl were common. There were some candidates who calculated the number of moles of Cl molecules (2.12/71) rather than Cl atoms.
notes.1f: Interpretation of data is an important skill at AS and A level. In this part many candidates confused the forces or bonds that would be broken when the solid is melted.
notes.1i: Most candidates knew or deduced that MgCl is an ionic solid.
notes.1ii: Fewer were able to deduce the bonding present in solid SbCl . This is a covalent solid. Many candidates were confused over the difference between these two.
notes.2a: Three equations were needed in the correct order starting from sulfur. The reactions were producing SO from S and O , producing SO from SO and O (which is reversible) and, finally, 2 2 3 2 2 forming H SO from SO and H O. Answers were generally correct with a small number of candidates writing unbalanced equations.
notes.2b: Examiners expected candidates to quote specific values of temperature and pressure rather than vague answers such as ‘low temperature’ or ‘high pressure’. Acceptable values were 400 to 600 oC and 1 to 10 atm., with units given. The catalyst had to be specified as vanadium(V) oxide by name or formula.
notes.2c: The best answers were specific, such as “making fertilizers”, and not vague such as “laboratory chemical”.
notes.2i: This was not well answered with many wrong equations involving nitric acid as a product.
notes.2ii: The environmental effects of acid rain were well known.
notes.2f: The fact that SO acts as a reducing agent in food preservation was known to about half the candidates.
notes.3i: Compound Z must have the molecular formula C H O. Candidates had to realise Z was ethanal, CH CHO, and not to write it as CH COH.
notes.3ii: The cyclic compound also has the molecular formula C H O and candidates were expected to deduce that there would be a 3 atom ring.
notes.3iii: The best answers to this part referred to the nitrogen atom forming two covalent bonds and having one lone pair so leaving an unpaired electron.
notes.3d: The best answers came from those candidates who realised that Acrolein has two functional groups which can react independently of one another and who decided what each functional group did in the reactions given. The most common error was in the last reaction where many candidates thought NaBH reduced both the –CHO and the >C=C< groups.
notes.4a: The majority of candidates were able to calculate the C:H:Br ratio as 3:7:1. The calculation to show that M = 122.9 was needed to prove that the empirical formula was the same as the molecular formula. Not all candidates did this.
notes.4i: Although many candidates knew that butan–1,4-diol would be formed a number failed to give the displayed formula as the question required.
notes.4ii: Fewer candidates were able to deduce that buta-1,4-diene would be produced and only a minority of candidates gave one of the two skeletal formulae. Information about drawing different types of structural formulae is given in Section 10.1 of the syllabus.
notes.4iii: Many candidates knew that ethanol is the solvent for this reaction.
notes.4iv: The majority of candidates knew that this is an elimination reaction.
notes.5b: Most candidates knew this precipitate was white.
notes.5c: The iodo- compound was usually identified here.
notes.5d: The fact that the C-I bond is the weakest needed to be supported by evidence from the Data Booklet as required in the question. notes.general_comments: General comments This paper tested candidates’ knowledge and understanding of important aspects of the AS Chemistry syllabus. Overall, there were many good answers to the paper and most candidates were able to demonstrate some positive achievement. Chemistry has a significant factual content and some of the questions asked candidates to recall their knowledge of the chemistry to be studied. There were many good answers to these questions but a number of candidates had not learned some basic chemistry. A large number of candidates struggled with one or both of the calculations, often because they did not use a logical method of answering the questions.
